picks.prediction: Florida Panthers moneyline. The Panthers arrive at the United Center at 5-4-2, with Brady Tkachuk already on seven goals, Matthew Tkachuk on twelve assists and Jacob Markstrom on three wins. Chicago's 3-7-0 start has produced three goals from its leading scorer, Roman Kantserov, so the visitors' top-line output looks the likelier source of the decisive goal.

Dallas Stars moneyline. Both clubs have played ten games; Dallas are 6-3-1 and the Islanders 5-3-2, and Dallas hold the better points rate on home ice. Mikko Rantanen's five goals and Jason Robertson's eight assists give the Stars two separate scoring routes in front of Jake Oettinger, who already has five wins, while New York lean on Ilya Sorokin's five wins and Bo Horvat's five goals.

Montreal Canadiens moneyline in the Heritage Classic. The NHL lists this as a neutral-site game at Princess Auto Stadium, which takes Winnipeg's home advantage out of the equation. Montreal are 5-3-2 with Cole Caufield on six goals and Nick Suzuki on seven assists; Winnipeg are 4-3-3, so the edge belongs to the Canadiens' slightly better points rate rather than to the venue.

Colorado Avalanche moneyline. Colorado are 6-4-1 against Nashville's 3-3-3, and the Avalanche carry the stronger scoring profile into Bridgestone Arena: Artturi Lehkonen has nine goals, Nathan MacKinnon thirteen assists and Mackenzie Blackwood five wins. Juuse Saros has three wins and Roman Josi eight assists for Nashville, but the Predators have won only three of their nine games.

Minnesota Wild moneyline. This is the widest record gap on the two-day slate: Minnesota are 6-3-2 with Kirill Kaprizov on eleven goals, Quinn Hughes on eleven assists and Jesper Wallstedt on six wins, while Vancouver are 2-9-1 and their leading scorer has four goals. Record, goaltending wins and top-line production all point the same way, which is why the price is short rather than generous.

Milwaukee Brewers moneyline. The Brewers finished the regular season 103-59 and lead this best-of-seven World Series 1-0 after game one. Logan Henderson is the home probable pitcher against Tampa Bay's Drew Rasmussen, and the Rays' 98-64 season was six wins lighter. Home field and the stronger season record make Milwaukee the side to take at American Family Field.

Saracens to win at the Twickenham Stoop. The official Gallagher PREM table has Saracens on 11 points from three rounds with a +21 points difference and a W-L-W sequence, against Harlequins' 2 points, -68 and three defeats. Saracens also start Fergus Burke at fly-half behind a pack captained by Maro Itoje; Harlequins have won the last two meetings at The Stoop, but the current table points one way.

Cucine Lube Civitanova moneyline. Civitanova opened the season with a 3-0 win at Verona, and Aleksandar Nikolov served five aces in it, the joint highest count published for round one. Padova were beaten 0-3 at home by Piacenza and did not reach 22 points in any set. The round-one table reads Civitanova 3, Padova 0.

Itas Trentino moneyline, and only on home floor. Trentino won 3-0 at Modena with Theo Faure scoring 23 points, the best single-match haul of the round. Cisterna answered with a 3-0 win over Milano, a 29-27 opening set and 13 blocks, eight of them from Shikun Peng. Both clubs sit on 3 points, so the venue carries this price.

Tinet Prata di Pordenone moneyline. Prata marked their return to the top division with a 3-1 win over Monza, Wout D'Heer scoring 18 points from the middle. Perugia, the reigning champions, needed five sets to see off Cuneo and collected 2 points. One round is a thin base, so this carries a Low grade and no more.

Vero Volley Monza moneyline, home floor only. Both clubs are on 0 points after one round: Monza lost 1-3 at Prata but took the second set 25-19, while Verona were swept 0-3 at home by Civitanova and won no set at all. With so little separating them the price is close to a coin flip, and the grade says so.
